# Temple Scroll Column 19 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 19 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**19:1** You shall then take the first ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the ram.

**19:2** You shall slaughter the ram, take its blood, and dash it against the altar on all sides.

**19:3** You shall cut the ram into its parts, wash its entrails and its legs,

**19:4** and arrange them with its other parts and its head.

**19:5** You shall turn the entire ram into smoke on the altar; it is a burnt offering to the LORD, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.

**19:6** Then you shall take the second ram — the ram of ordination —

**19:7** and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the ram.

**19:8** You shall slaughter the ram and take some of its blood and apply it to the lobe of Aaron's right ear,

**19:9** to the lobe of the right ear of each of his sons, to the thumb of their right hand, and to the big toe of their right foot.

**19:10** You shall dash the remaining blood against the altar on all sides.

**19:11** Then you shall take some of the blood that is on the altar and some of the anointing oil and sprinkle it on Aaron and on his vestments,

**19:12** and on his sons and on the vestments of his sons with him; and he shall be consecrated — he and his vestments, and his sons and their vestments with him.

**19:13** You shall take from the ram the fat, the fat tail, the fat covering the entrails,

**19:14** the appendage of the liver, the two kidneys with the fat on them, and the right thigh — for it is a ram of ordination —

**19:15** and one loaf of bread, one cake of oiled bread, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before Me.

---

*LOGOS notes: Column 19 is well preserved, paralleling Exodus 29:15-23. The two-ram sequence distinguishes the burnt offering (first ram, entirely consumed on the altar) from the ordination offering (second ram, with distinctive blood application). The ear-thumb-toe rite (19:8-9) symbolically consecrates the priests' hearing, working, and walking. The sprinkling of mixed blood and oil (19:11) creates a unique consecration medium. "Before Me" replaces "before the LORD" in the Temple Scroll's characteristic reformulation.*
